description: Recent struggles for racial justice have reignited debates about how US history should be told. Do we have one cohesive history? Whose stories should we tell and why? Who gets to choose? This course explores these questions by analyzing recent attempts to create and present a national history, such as the 1619 Project, which foregrounds the introduction of slavery to North America and the 1776 Commission, which locates patriotism as an essential element of history education. At its core, this course asks students to consider what history is and the ways it often functions as a space of conflict for the present and the future.
